answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create: an agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time. New identities start at the bottom of the delta between cheap entry and earned standing, a canyon no attacker crosses for free, since spinning up thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of deposits. A prism of independent attestations then refracts that history: peers score real output, and identities with no verifiable record stay invisible to the economy.
